data.gender_notes: Adityan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Adityan is the name of the Sun God in Hindu mythology. He is also known as Surya and is considered the god of energy, life, and strength. The name Adityan is derived from Aditya, which means 'sun' in Sanskrit. The name Adityan carries the meaning “Sun God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Adityan usually hope their child will grow to embody sun god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Adityan is a significant name in Hindu culture, representing the Sun God, who is a crucial deity in Hinduism. In Hindu traditions, the Sun is revered as the source of all life. The Sun God is honored with various rituals, prayers, and festivals throughout the year, particularly during the auspicious festival of Diwali. Adityan is a name that carries the deep-rooted respect for the Sun God in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Adityan, as the name of the Sun God, holds immense spiritual significance in Hinduism. The Sun God is considered the ultimate symbol of energy, creativity, and life force. Worshipping Adityan helps in the spiritual growth of an individual by bringing positivity, happiness, and divine blessings into one's life. The Sun God is also believed to be the dispenser of justice, and the light of knowledge, as represented by the Sun's rays. Adityan is thus a powerful name that is deeply connected to the spiritual beliefs and practices within the Hindu tradition.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adityan signifies the embodiment of the radiant and supreme sun god, Aditya, in an individual. It symbolizes enlightenment, illumination, and the power to dispel darkness and ignorance.

vedic_reference.note: Adityan is a name of the Sun God in Hindu mythology, and is mentioned in various Vedic texts. He is also known as Surya and Ravi.

historical_references.reference: Adityan is a name of the Hindu solar deity Surya, which means 'the sun'. The name Adityan is derived from Aditya, which means 'radiant, shining, or having light'. Aditya was one of the twelve Adityas or 'shining ones' in Hindu mythology, who were the divine sons of the god Aditi, or 'boundless'. Each Aditya had a specific role and was associated with a particular aspect of the sun. Adityan, as the name of the solar deity, represents the shining or radiant aspect of the sun. This name was in use during the Vedic period, around 1500-500 BCE.

Adityan is also a name of the Hindu god Rudra, who is a form of Shiva. In this context, Adityan is represented as the 'sun-god' Rudra. This association of Rudra with the sun is seen in the Rigveda, where Rudra is referred to as 'Surya' and 'Pusan', two other names of the sun-god. The name Adityan for Rudra is derived from Aditya, which is also the name of the sun-god. This association of Rudra with the sun emphasizes his role as a creator and destroyer, as the sun brings life and also causes destruction through heat.

modern_usage.modern_context: Adityan, a name of the Hindu sun god Aditya, has gained popularity in modern contexts across various platforms. In the realm of spirituality, Adityan is embraced in yoga and meditation studios, symbolizing the radiant and enlightening qualities of the sun god. Lastly, in the context of globalization, it is used in international schools to provide a diverse range of names and religious traditions to students.
